reason: The passage contains three explicitly named characters: Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה), Moses (מֹשֶׁה), and God/YHWH (יְהוָה). All three occupy leadership positions—Pharaoh as king of Egypt, Moses as leader of the Israelites, and God as the ultimate divine authority directing events. Other entities mentioned (the people, the Israelites, the Egyptians, Pharaoh's servants, the Angel of God) are either collective groups without individual names or functionally described beings rather than named characters. The Angel of God, while mentioned, is identified only by role rather than given a proper name.
